sourceInformation.source: Solaris (1986), Atari 2600; created by Doug Neubauer
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade space shooter with strategic sector navigation
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person chase view, with a galactic scanner
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer, TSL, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, AI Hub session client 1.4.0, WebRTC, BroadcastChannel; esbuild 0.25.12 for packaging
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural 3D cel shading, geometric ink outlines, lavender alien landscapes, mint thrusters and warm coral enemies; space-comic typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for thrusters, barrel rolls, cadet waving, enemy limbs, ion doors and reactor pulses; procedural flight and particle motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only Web Audio arpeggiated synth music at 10% default volume, synthesized cannons, explosions, pickups, engines and UI sounds; Animalese-style gibberish radio
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Protocol v1 ghost races for 1–4 pilots; standalone BroadcastChannel wing races for up to four tabs on the same origin, and direct two-device WebRTC invitation/answer exchange
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with software WebGPU; scripted full campaign; simulated standard gamepad; landscape touch profile; Web Audio analyser; offline file URL; two-page BroadcastChannel and WebRTC; AI Hub two- and four-player harness with latency, jitter, packet loss and host departure. WebGL2 screenshots for visual review. Physical controller, native mobile hardware and wide-area NAT compatibility unknown. No FPS target.
sourceInformation.research: Original Atari Solaris manual, Doug Neubauer's Atari history, AtariAge screenshots and gameplay captures; documented alarm and combat sound cues; exact original sound timbres unknown. Official Three.js and Rapier docs, local versioned APIs, and AI Hub Protocol v1 README and harness.

testingFeedback: Testing and visual review caught five distinct game issues: a Rapier lifetime crash, a multi-canvas shader warmup hang, an unstarted music sequencer, a weak flagship silhouette and small flight prompts. Two test fixture mistakes also caused false failures. All were corrected.
Two were game breaking: the long-playthrough physics crash and multiplayer startup hang.
The scripted six-sector playthrough through real Rapier hits and pickups, followed by the AI Hub four-pilot lossy-network and host-leave checks.
The headless WebGPU screenshot was blank despite the game running. State checks verified WebGPU; WebGL2 screenshots were useful for visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL made the same cel-shading materials work on WebGPU and the WebGL2 fallback; AnimationMixer gave the procedural models a reusable animation base.

Yes. Reusing a physics world across encounter changes failed in the long playthrough, and awaiting shader warmup stalled simultaneous WebGPU copies. Fresh encounter worlds, collision filters and first-render shader compilation resolved the tested failures.
The encounter-driven campaign, sector progression, controller-focus navigation, assisted touch input and ghost-race state management.
Coordinating GPU startup, fixed-step physics lifetimes and multiple game copies in headless tests.
Clearer diagnostics and a more predictable shader-compilation lifecycle for several simultaneous WebGPU canvases.
promptFeedback: The concrete controller, touch, attract-mode, developer-tools and Hub requirements made the intended finish line clear.
The expected standalone multiplayer connection method was unspecified. I provided same-origin tab races and direct WebRTC invitations. Exact original sound timbres remain unknown.
Combining six distinct encounters, procedural cel-shaded art, code-only audio and verified networking in one self-contained HTML file.
Specify the intended demo length and the desired standalone multiplayer connection workflow.

aiHub.name: Solar Mayhem
aiHub.description: A cel-shaded chase-view space adventure inspired by Solaris. Break a raiding fleet, rescue cadets, slip through an ion corridor and take the stolen sun back from the Nightjar.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick / mouse / touch drag to fly; Space / click / R2 fire; Shift / Cross boost; E / Square pulse; Q / Circle roll; Tab / Triangle scanner; Esc / Options pause.
